title: Superconductivity in High-Entropy Alloy System Containing Tb.

recollection.starting_material: Likely a mixture of multiple elements including terbium (Tb), possibly other rare earths or transition metals.
recollection.intervention: Synthesis of a high-entropy alloy (HEA) by mixing and melting several elements to form a single-phase solid solution.
recollection.structure: Probably a crystalline solid solution with a random distribution of constituent elements, characteristic of HEAs.
recollection.mechanism: Superconductivity may arise due to electron pairing facilitated by the unique electronic structure of the HEA, possibly influenced by the presence of Tb and other elements.
recollection.results: Main quantitative results likely include the superconducting transition temperature (Tc), possibly in the low-temperature range (below 10 K), and characterization of the phase purity and composition.

score.note: The recollection gives only a generic HEA melting/synthesis description and a generic random solid-solution structure, missing the specific Tb addition to a defined Tb-free matrix, the bcc lattice changes, and Tb/Tb2O3 secondary phases. Its proposed superconducting mechanism is speculative and does not capture the observed degradation or the paper's mechanistic uncertainty. No numerical values close to the reported Tc, Hc2, heat-capacity jump, or coupling parameters are provided.
